items.summary: If you haven't already, check out FabCon and SQLCon 2026 in Barcelona: Building the data foundation for Microsoft Copilot and Agents for a complete look at all of our FabCon Europe announcements across Fabric and Microsoft Databases. Advancing an open, interoperable semantic foundation for AI-powered analytics Today, Microsoft is pleased to affirm our commitment to Apache Ossie (incubating) , a community-led effort to establish a vendor-neutral standard for exchanging semantic metadata across analytics, AI, and BI platforms. This has been a close collaboration with Snowflake, who helped found Ossie . We have heard loud and clear that customers want to enable platform-agnostic agentic experiences. Shared semantic context must be defined once and reused across platforms, enabling agentic consumption at scale, maximizing the reach of AI-powered analytics, and empowering users to leverage the best agent for the job. Power BI semantic models are key enablers of AI-powered analysis, providing humans and AI agents with governed semantic context to answer data questions quickly and confidently. items.title: Power BI’s next chapter: The evolution of business intelligence
items.summary: If you haven't already, check out FabCon and SQLCon 2026 in Barcelona: Building the data foundation for Microsoft Copilot and Agents for a complete look at all of our FabCon Europe announcements across Fabric and Microsoft Databases. More than a decade ago, I watched Power BI change the way users work, analyze and take action on their data. Since then, I have had the privilege of seeing it grow alongside our customers—from a tool for building reports into a platform used by millions of people to understand their businesses and make decisions every day. Now, Power BI is entering its next chapter. Introducing the next generation of report development We’re introducing a new app building experience in Power BI Desktop, powered by apps in Fabric , that enables users to create data applications using natural language. Starting from a trusted semantic model, users can generate, preview, edit, and publish purpose-built applications to Microsoft Fabric. These applications can accept inputs, write back data, preserve shared state, and support operational workflows, helping users move from insight to action. items.summary: This release is part of the broader ODBC-to-ADBC transition for Power Query connectors described in the Transition from ODBC to ADBC drivers in Power BI and Microsoft Fabric documentation. What’s new Existing connections in your semantic models, dataflows, and paginated reports continue to work unchanged — the migration path is currently opt-in per connection, per workspace, or per tenant. Highlights: Improved security - ADBC drivers incorporate security enhancements, such as memory safety and garbage collection. No changes to existing behavior - This transition moves away from the embedded ODBC drivers that ship with Power BI. It does not change behavior for the ODBC connector when you use a separately installed ODBC driver. Efficient large dataset support - ADBC provides a set of standard interfaces for interacting with Arrow data, which is especially efficient at fetching large datasets with minimal overhead and no serialization or copying. Supported authentication - Databricks ADBC supports OAuth (user), OAuth (M2M / Client Credentials), and Microsoft Entra ID.
